newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: China's premier signs energy deals in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: China's premier signs energy deals in Venezuela.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng, stressing China's desire to boost trade ties with Latin America, signed energy supply deals with oil-rich Venezuela Wednesday.

Li, on the last leg of a regional tour that also took him to Chile and Brazil, signed with President Rafael Caldera agreements on the supply of local trademark Orimulsion boiler fuel to China and a possible $320-million joint venture production plant.
"For China, relations with Latin America are of great importance," Li said in a brief speech. "Eloquent proof of that is the signing of these cooperation agreements."
Li and Caldera signed a memorandum of understanding for a feasibility study on an Orimulsion plant in eastern Venezuela.

The study is due to be completed by the middle of next year. If approved, the plant would go on stream in late 1999, producing about five million tonnes of the extra heavy bitumen-type oil for the Chinese market only.
Another agreement was for the shipment of 140,000 tonnes of Orimulsion, as part of on-going tests on the boiler fuel alternative in China that began in August.
Li was expected to spell out China's policy towards Latin America Thursday in an address to the Latin American Economic System (SELA), a Caracas-based regional economic think-tank.

Trade between China and Latin America and the Caribbean nearly tripled in five years to reach $6 billion in 1995, SELA figures show. But more than a third of these commercial exchanges were with Brazil, Latin America's largest country.
On the diplomatic front, an accord was also signed Thursday to maintain a Venezuelan consulate in Hong Kong when the British colony is handed back to Beijing next July.
Venezuelan government sources said Caldera raised the human rights issue during his meeting with Li but they gave no details.
China's policy on this, as reiterated by Li in Santiago de Chile last week, is that Beijing accepts no foreign interference in domestic issues.
